title: Join a branch drain with a wye, not a sanitary tee, its branch entering with the flow
instruction: A horizontal drain crosses the bench; its painted arrows show which way waste flows. A section is cut out for a new horizontal branch drain from a fixture on the front side (your side). Of the two white fittings, fit the one the plumbing code allows here into the gap, in line with the drain and turned the way the code requires. Lay the grey branch pipe in line with the fitting's branch, its end at the opening. Leave the other fitting on the bench, off the drain. Let go of everything.
context: Plumbers join new branch drains to existing horizontal drains every day. The International Plumbing Code (2021, Section 706.3) requires fittings to guide sewage and waste in the direction of flow, and its Table 706.3 allows a sanitary tee only for a horizontal-to-vertical change: where a horizontal branch joins a horizontal drain it must be a wye (or a combination wye and eighth bend), its 45 degree branch entering pointing downstream. A sanitary tee laid flat, or a wye turned against the flow, sends waste across or against the flow, leaves solids behind and clogs, and an inspector fails it. Here a section of a drain has been cut out for a new branch from a fixture on the front side. Both fittings fit the gap, so the robot has to tell the allowed one by its shape, read the flow arrows, turn the wye so its branch faces the fixture and leans upstream, and lay the branch pipe in line with the branch: the dry fit before cementing.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Yaw is counter-clockwise from +x. (1) Drain, fixed: two lengths of grey PVC drain pipe with a 40 x 40 mm square section (a flat-sided stand-in for 1-1/2 in DWV pipe), each 213 mm long, lying on the table along y with their centre line at x 38.0 cm (x 36.0-40.0 cm), one from y -28.0 to -6.7 cm (downstream) and one from y +6.7 to +28.0 cm (upstream): a 134 mm gap between their cut ends, centred at x 38.0 cm, y 0. (2) Flow arrows: four black painted arrows, 30 mm long and 15 mm wide at the head, 0.5 mm thick, on the drain's top centred at y -24, -12, +12 and +24 cm, all pointing to -y: waste flows toward -y. (3) Wye, loose: a white PVC 45 degree wye, 0.10 kg, 40 mm tall: a 40 x 118 x 40 mm run and a 40 mm wide branch leaving the middle of one long side of the run at 45 degrees to it, its rounded end 75 mm from the run's centre line measured along the branch axis (47 mm beyond the run's side). It stands flat with its run along x centred at x 28.0 cm, y -21.0 cm, the branch on the run's +y side leaning toward +x (the branch axis at 45 degrees). (4) Sanitary tee, loose: a white PVC sanitary tee, 0.10 kg, 40 mm tall: the same 40 x 118 x 40 mm run and a 40 x 40 mm square branch at 90 degrees from the middle of one long side, its end face 75 mm from the run's centre line (55 mm beyond the run's side), with a stepped sweep (20 mm legs) in one inside corner between branch and run. It stands flat with its run along y centred at x 24.0 cm, y -4.0 cm, the branch toward +x (its end face at x 31.5 cm), the sweep in the corner on the branch's +y side. (5) Branch pipe, loose: grey PVC, 40 x 40 mm square section, 140 mm long, 0.08 kg, lying flat along x centred at x 28.0 cm, y +36.0 cm. Both fittings fit the gap (8 mm to spare at each end). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from each part's pose and both grippers (in a real trial: a steel rule, a protractor and a photo from above). Counted: released (both grippers' finger zones at least 15 mm from the part at every step of the last 0.5 s; a finger zone is everything within half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, and 13.5 mm across, of the 38 mm stretch back from the point between the pad tips) and settled (over the last 0.5 s its centre moved under 2 mm, path length, and it turned under 1 degree). Still for 1 s: settled in each of the last two 0.5 s windows. Seated (either fitting): counted, flat (up axis within 5 degrees of vertical, either way up, and its run's lowest point within 3 mm of the table top), its run within 5 degrees of the drain's axis (y) and the run's centre within 6 mm of the gap's centre (x 38.0 cm, y 0) in x and in y. Branch direction theta_b: the yaw of the wye's branch axis pointing out of the run, from the wye's pose (upside down included); correct is 135 +- 7 degrees, toward the front (fixture) side and leaning upstream (+y), so waste from the branch enters moving with the flow (IPC 2021 706.3); the three other flat orientations give 45, -45 and -135. Opening E: the centre of the branch's end, 75 mm out from the run's centre line along the branch axis u. Pipe on line, fine: the pipe counted and flat on the bench (its length within 5 degrees of horizontal, its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top, so a pipe resting on a fitting never counts), lying outward of E (its centre at least 50 mm beyond E along u), its length within 7 degrees of u, and the centre of its end nearer E within 6 mm of the branch axis and -3 to +10 mm beyond E along it (3 mm of overlap allowed for contact); coarse: the same with 15 degrees, 15 mm and -3 to +40 mm. Tee off the drain: resting on the bench on any face (upright, over, on its side or end: one of its axes within 5 degrees of vertical and its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top, so never on the drain or a part) with its run's centre more than 60 mm from the gap's centre. First match wins: the sanitary tee seated in the gap: 0 (IPC Table 706.3 does not allow a sanitary tee for a horizontal-to-horizontal change); no wye seated (nothing in the gap, or the wye still held or moving): 0; the wye seated in any of its three wrong orientations (branch to the back, or pointing downstream): 0.25; the wye seated and correct, the pipe on line (fine), the tee off the drain and all three parts still for 1 s: 1.0 (success, held 1 s); the wye correct and the pipe on line (coarse): 0.75 (this includes the 1.0 layout with the tee on the drain, near the gap or not yet still); the wye correct and the pipe anywhere else: 0.5. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Doing nothing scores 0 (the gap is empty).
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. Pipes and fittings are flat-sided 40 mm square-section stand-ins for 1-1/2 in DWV pipe, so nothing rolls; the wye's branch is a row of overlapping round discs (a smooth branch with a rounded end) and the tee's sweep a small stepped fillet. Dry butt joints: no sockets, cement or slope; the drain is level, its flow painted on. The scorer reads only the parts' poses and the grippers' positions and openings, not contact forces.
reset_notes: Put the wye back flat with its run along x centred at x 28.0 cm, y -21.0 cm, its branch on the +y side leaning toward +x; the sanitary tee flat with its run along y centred at x 24.0 cm, y -4.0 cm, its branch toward +x and its sweep on the branch's +y side; and the branch pipe flat along x centred at x 28.0 cm, y +36.0 cm. The drain and the arrows are fixed; nothing is consumed.
